newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dock strike cripples Bangladesh port for fourth day.
newsitem.headline: Dock strike cripples Bangladesh port for fourth day.

text.p: A violent strike by dock workers crippled Bangladesh's main Chittagong port for a fourth day on Sunday and officials said only intervention by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina could break the stalemate.
"It looks like dragging on until the prime minister intervenes to solve the dispute. The efforts by Chittagong Port Authority have so far failed," said one port official.

Hasina, now on a visit to Japan, is expected to return home later on Sunday. Ten people were injured on Saturday after rival workers clashed with knives and home-made bombs outside the port. Nearly 8,000 dock workers walked off the job on Thursday after a dispute triggered by attempts to allow coaster hatch workers to work on the jetties by the port authorities.

Coaster hatch workers, who are not listed as port workers, normally handle only cargo for small local ships outside the port. These workers are now seeking jobs in the port, and registered dock workers fear losing their jobs as a result.
Port officials say the problem is continuing because the government leaders are divided over the dispute.

Influential local leader and Chittagong City Mayor A.B.M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury is backing the demand of the coaster hatch workers for jobs on the port while Shipping Minister A.S.M. Abdur Rab refuses to provide jobs for them.
There were about 33 ships at the port jetties and at the outer anchorage awaiting loading and unloading of cargo, the officials said.
They said nearly 150,000 tonnes of cargo had also piled up at the port because of the strike.
